title: New to Game Dev - Advisories
author: CmdrCallandra
selftext:
Hi,

Am new to game development, just drafted my first game design document and am now thinking about strategies to implement. Being solo one of my main issues will be in creating game assets. Do you have any recommendations? Know of AI tools that can help me here too?

Any help is greatly appreciated.

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body: Find cheap assets, buy them online, or try the painstaking process of having AI try to make them. It depends on what you are making. Humble Bundle has an amazing Unreal Engine asset pack they are selling for like US$20

comments.author: mapachegram
comments.body: Yo estoy en la misma que vos, pude avanzar mucho gracias a los agentes de Google, antigravity, junto con unity y nano banana para los gráficos, nano banana funciona muy bien si le das una referencia así que lo que yo te recomiendo es que compres assets y los modifiques con ia para tener recursos infinitos, así es como estoy trabajando en mi tiempo libre es muy divertido al tener agentes trabajando con vos no te sentis tan solitario en la creación de tu proyecto, de echo a veces el agente esta mas entusiasmado que yo en el proyecto.

comments.author: HealthyWest6482
comments.body: depends on the game type. my first project I opted for a turn-based classic RPG because of this exact thought lol. many free assets available though - itch is pretty good especially for sprites.

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body: Have fun and enjoy the process. You will not make any money soon snd your first game will suck in others eyes but you will and should be proud. Try to find like minded and collaborate, it’s a great way to learn. Game Jams are great way to learn and force you to make smaller games.

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: And yes Claude code is awesome but costly. Use MCPs and use AI to both develop and learn.

replies.author: CmdrCallandra
replies.body:
Thanks for the advice. I am closing in to finish my first real Claude code project which was initially thought to be a test run but that kinda snowballed into 93k lines of code and still going. 
So I am quite confident that I will be able to at least create a working PoC with CC and from there I gonna see how good I can implement my design document that I already wrote together. 

Pretty fascinating times to be in honestly..

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: That is impressive. My Experian is that when hitting more than 10k lines architecture start to become important and after 20k testing and good development skill is important. Do you have any thing to show? Also did you learn some strategy that did work?

replies.author: CmdrCallandra
replies.body:
Thanks, I do have a strong IT background, so I know about project planning, phases milestones etc. I did ask quite intense planning session first to pin down the first 10 to 12 milestones to get the core functionality, then had more ideas which got me to 20+ milestones now. I copy in the initial description from my quite long readme about my project..

DAWAI combines FL Studio's visual layout, Ableton's arrangement + session workflow, and AI-powered generation/separation tools into a single local-first application. Built with Svelte 5, Tone.js, Fastify, and TailwindCSS 4.

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: That makes sense. You are 100% on right track. The major problem you will find in game dev is that AI is bad crossing the layers like in unity moving from code to components on gameobjects and then back. I believe Godot have a benefit for being pure text. But unity is stronger and more powerful. You can go without engine and just use a framework. I’m heavy in to Unity and multiplayer VR development just for context.
